main_point: Startup web broadcaster Joost has secured a deal with Warner Brothers to host content, positioning itself as a key player in the emerging online TV market by combining consumer demand for flexibility with industry interests in content control.

statements.text: The startup web broadcaster Joost has signed a deal with Warner Brothers to host content, a move that establishes the company as a primary aggregator in the developing online television sector by bridging the gap between viewer demand for flexibility and media companies' need for content control.
statements.text_short: Joost's partnership with Warner Brothers establishes it as a key aggregator in online TV.

statements.text: Viewers of the online television service can interact with programming through integrated widgets such as clocks, instant messaging, news feeds, and chat rooms, while retaining the ability to disable these features if they prefer a standard viewing experience.
statements.text_short: Users can interact with online TV programming via customizable widgets.

statements.text: Despite initial controversies and legal challenges, online broadband peer-to-peer connectivity represents a permanent shift in media distribution that will continue to evolve and reshape how content is delivered to consumers globally.
statements.text_short: Media distribution has undergone a permanent change toward online peer-to-peer connectivity.

statements.text: The leadership of the startup web broadcaster Joost asserts that the service successfully combines the consumer desire for flexible, on-demand viewing with the entertainment industry's requirement to retain control over their intellectual property, creating a viable business model for the future of online television.
statements.text_short: Joost's leadership claims to balance consumer flexibility with industry content control.

statements.actor: established subscription cable and satellite distribution channels
actor_aliases: established subscription cable and satellite distribution channels
statements.text: The new online TV platform currently lacks the highest quality programming available through established subscription cable and satellite distribution channels, meaning early users must accept a trade-off between the convenience of web-based viewing and superior broadcast fidelity.
statements.text_short: Established subscription cable and satellite distribution channels offer the highest quality programming. The new online TV platform does not have this level of content.

statements.text: Internet TV includes an 'on-demand' option that saves room in the distribution pipeline. This feature also sends data back to the aggregator, showing precisely which items are popular. As a result, it creates a better content distribution model than current systems.
statements.text_short: Internet TV includes an 'on-demand' option. This option saves room in the distribution pipeline. It also sends data back to the aggregator. This data shows exactly what content people want.

statements.text: This new web broadcaster model allows a middle-man to negotiate with media conglomerates and handle a stream of content that has not been watched, which helps save network bandwidth.
statements.text_short: This new web broadcasting approach allows an intermediary to bargain with media conglomerates and handle a stream of content that has not yet been watched.

statements.text: This web broadcaster allows users to choose free online television shows. The service handles the content deals and serves as a portal to the programs, offering a fresh way for viewers to access them.
statements.text_short: This web broadcaster allows users to choose free online television shows based on content deals the service has made.
